Site includes a privately maintained detention/biofiltration pond for stormwater management. Once the maintenance agreement is formally recorded, the document number must be added to the cover sheet.

Legal description shows the subdivision volume and page (Volume 73, Page 76, Mecey Subdivision), but the instrument or document recording number is not included. Complete final plat recording information including document/instrument number must be referenced per UCM 2.5.1.E.13.

comment: Multiple non-cover sheets (Sheets 2, 9, 12 verified; others not individually examined) do not reserve a blank space in the lower right corner for batch stamping. Full approval blocks and other content must be removed from the batch-stamp area to ensure space is reserved for City use.

Applicant (Jason Rodgers, P.E., Bleyl Engineering) is not the property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC). A separate owner's authorization letter or authorization form from the record owner authorizing the applicant to submit on behalf of the owner is not clearly evident in the submittal package.

Owner is a legal entity (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC) with signatory identified as Authorized Signer (Richard D. Agnew), but documentation proving the signatory's authority to bind the entity (corporate resolution, operating agreement extract, partnership resolution, trust document, or similar) is not provided in the submittal.

Warranty deed is not submitted as a supporting document in the application package, although the application references deed Document Number 2019197883. The recorded warranty deed establishing current ownership of the subject property must be provided.

Sheet 9 title block shows SP-2023-0126C per vision analysis, but official documentation states SP-2025-0126C. The site plan number format SP-XXXX-XXXX appears correct where visible, but the year discrepancy between sheets (2023 vs 2025) cannot be verified without examining the actual source document. Landscape sheets 30-31 use project number format (013-25-01) instead of SP-XXXX-XXXX format.

comment: Scale verification completed for plan sheets (1" = 20') and location map (1" = 400'), but utility plan-profile sheets (19-20) and standard details sheets (23-28) were not examined visually to confirm scale legibility and format on all sheets.

Sheet sizes confirmed as 24" × 36" for Sheets 21-22. However, sheet sizes for utility sheets 19-20 and landscape sheets 30-31 (which show inconsistent numbering 27-28 of 35) were not verified. Landscape sheets may be from a separate document set with different sizing standards.

Location map exists on cover sheet with north arrow, but visual clarity and whether site location is sufficiently clear relative to surrounding context could not be fully verified without examining the source document.

The primary site plan (Sheet 9) does not clearly distinguish existing conditions from proposed development. While Sheet 4 shows existing conditions and Sheet 8 shows demolition, the main Site Plan (Sheet 9) does not use consistent visual treatment (colors, line weights, symbols, labeling, or graying) to distinguish proposed buildings and improvements from any existing conditions that remain or are referenced. Linework and features lack clear visual segregation.
applicableAreas: Overall site plan sheets and proposed development sheets

comment: Sheets 13-14 are listed as drainage area maps, but visual examination of whether base impervious cover, redeveloped impervious cover, and new impervious cover are shown with distinct shading and clear labeling could not be verified from the available text descriptions.
applicableAreas: Drainage area maps and impervious cover exhibits

comment: Sheet 4 is labeled 'Existing Conditions Survey' and the guide indicates it shows existing topography and existing conditions. However, visual verification that the sheet reflects current (not proposed) grades and layout, and whether it is clearly distinguished from the demolition plan, requires examination of the actual source document.

Property boundary bearings show inconsistencies across sheets: Sheet 9 shows N62°36'57"W, Sheet 8 shows N63°39'57"W, and Sheet 29 shows N63°36'57"W for nominally the same boundary segment. Verify that all property boundary dimensions and bearings match the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) and resolve discrepancies with clarification notes or a revised survey.

Multiple distinct easement types are shown on the site plan sheets (Drainage Easement, Wastewater Easement, Water Easement/Vault Easement, Sidewalk Easement, Public Utility Easement, Electric Easement), but the legend defines only a generic 'Easement' symbol (dashed line with PUE text). Each easement type shown on the plans must have its own defined linetype and symbol in the legend to clearly differentiate easement categories.

The Right-of-Way (ROW) boundary symbol is not included in the site plan legend. UCM 2.5.1.E.9 requires ROW dimensions and legend definitions on all Austin Water civil plan sheets. Add ROW boundary linetype and symbol to the legend.

The legend defines only the City of Austin 100-year floodplain ('100 yr' linetype) but does not separately define the FEMA floodplain linetype. LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) requires both the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and the FEMA floodplain to be depicted with distinct, defined linetypes in the plan legend. Add FEMA floodplain symbol and linetype to the legend, clearly distinguished from the local 100-year floodplain.

Neither the City of Austin 100-year floodplain boundary nor the FEMA floodplain boundary is depicted as delineated linework on any site plan sheet. Although the project location is outside the 100-year floodplain (FEMA Zone X per cover sheet), LDC § 25-7-33(D)(3) explicitly requires every site plan—including those outside floodplain areas—to affirmatively show (a) the City of Austin 100-year floodplain and (b) the FEMA floodplain as distinct delineated boundaries with linework, not merely in the legend. Add both floodplain boundaries to the appropriate plan sheets with distinct, defined linetypes.

Buildings are labeled with unit numbers only (e.g., 'Unit 101', 'Unit 102') on the site plan and addressing plan sheets. UCM 2.5.1.E.14 requires the street address for all existing and proposed structures to appear on the lot(s) where structures are located on Austin Water utility plan sheets. For this multi-family project with 39 units, each building footprint must be labeled with its assigned street address in the format: 3759 Valley View Road, Unit [number] (or equivalent format confirmed with Address Management Services).
applicableAreas: Site plan, addressing plan, and all applicable building footprints

comment: Land Area Calculation (LOC) number is not included in or associated with the Site Data Table. The table shows a separate 'Site Area Calculation (MF-2)' for unit-count requirements but no LOC identifier.

No separate table is provided on the site plan sheet showing the total area within the limits of construction. The cover sheet indicates 2.26 acres for limits of construction but no detailed calculation table is presented on the site plan sheet.

Minimum site area required per MF-2 zoning is not shown in the Site Data Table. The requirement of 93,600 sf (for 39 units × 2,400 sf/unit) appears only in a separate 'Site Area Calculation (MF-2)' table, not in the main SDT.
Individual building GFA values are not shown in the Site Data Table. Building-by-building GFA is documented in an adjacent Building Data Table (Block 15), not within the SDT itself as required.

Floor-to-area ratio (FAR) is completely missing from the Site Data Table. Although total GFA (83,986 sf) and site area (94,192 sf) are shown, no FAR value or ratio is provided. FAR should be expressed as a ratio (e.g., 0.89:1).

Neither proposed FAR nor maximum allowed FAR per LDC § 25-2-492 is shown in the SDT. FAR is absent from all site plan tables and must be added with comparison to the maximum allowable FAR for the MF-2 district.
FAR value cannot be verified because FAR is not shown in the SDT. Therefore, reconciliation between the stated FAR and the calculation of GFA divided by site area cannot be confirmed.
Open space is shown in square feet (required 4,709.62 sf / provided 4,710 sf) but the percentage is not shown. The requirement specifies both square feet and percentage must be displayed in the SDT.

Open space areas are required to be delineated on the site plan sheet. Visual delineation of specific open space areas cannot be confirmed from the submitted document analysis without explicit identification on the drawing.

Building height is not shown in the Site Data Table. While a separate Building Height Table shows stories (max 3) and heights in feet (33'-4.75" to 36'-1"), this information is located in an adjacent table, not within the SDT as required.

Both proposed and maximum allowed building height are not shown in the Site Data Table. Building height information appears in an adjacent Building Height Table (showing individual building heights and 40' maximum), not consolidated in the SDT itself.

Foundation type is documented as a single project-wide value (Slab on Grade) rather than documented per individual building. If all buildings share the same foundation type, this should be explicitly stated per building or documented separately for each.

Finished floor elevation (FFE) per building is not documented in the Site Data Table. FFE values (ranging from 680.50 to 687.50) are labeled on the Grading Plan for each building but do not appear in the SDT as required.

Maximum elevation permitted by zoning is not shown in the SDT or compared alongside the proposed FFE for each building. A comparison table must be provided to demonstrate compliance of proposed FFE against the zoning height district maximums.
applicableAreas: Site Data Table and Grading Plan, Sheets 9 and 11

comment: The SDT does not show both proposed and maximum allowed values for all applicable fields. Specifically, FAR (both proposed and maximum) and building height (both proposed and maximum) are missing from the SDT, appearing only in adjacent separate tables.

Verification of correct GFA definition application requires detailed floor plans showing: all areas with >6 feet clear height, inclusion of loading docks, exclusion of atria airspace above ground floor, exclusion of parking facilities and driveways, and exclusion of enclosed loading berths and off-street maneuvering areas. Sufficient detail is not available in submitted documents.

Verification that building coverage correctly excludes ground level paving, landscaping, open recreational facilities, incidental projecting eaves, balconies, and similar features requires detailed building elevation and footprint analysis. Sufficient documentation is not available in submitted drawings.
applicableAreas: Building elevations and site plan, Sheet 9

comment: Verification that the impervious cover calculation does not improperly apply the 2-foot projecting element exemption requires review of detailed IC worksheets (Q1/Q2 calculation tables). These worksheets showing element-by-element IC accounting are not included in the submitted documents.

Unit type breakdown table does not provide the comprehensive format required for parking calculations. Current documentation shows 16 Two Bedroom and 23 Three Bedroom units but lacks a formal zero-based table with columns for studio/efficiency, 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, 3-bedroom, and total counts. This table is required to enable quick verification of parking requirements by bedroom type per Appendix A.
applicableAreas: Building Data Table on Site Plan

comment: Total bedroom count for the entire development is not explicitly documented. While the count can be calculated from unit breakdown (16 two-bedroom units + 23 three-bedroom units = 101 total bedrooms), it must be directly stated in the site plan documentation for clarity. Parking requirement calculations in Appendix A reference bedroom count, making this a critical data point.
applicableAreas: Building Data Table on Site Plan

comment: Proposed floor area ratio is 0.891:1 (gross floor area 83,986 sf ÷ site area 94,192 sf), which exceeds the MF-2 zoning maximum of 0.5:1 per LDC § 25-2-492. No approved variance, density bonus, or other exemption is documented on the site plan or in supplementary applications. Either reduce the proposed gross floor area to achieve a compliant FAR of 0.5:1 or lower, or submit documentation of an approved variance from the Board of Adjustment.

Site Data Table identifies use as 'Multi-Family Residential' which is not a specific LDC-defined use name. All proposed uses must be identified using exact terminology from LDC § 25-2-3 (Multifamily Residential, Condominium Residential, or Townhouse Residential), not generic variations with hyphens or capitalization differences. Update Site Data Table and application to specify the exact LDC-defined residential use sub-type.

Residential use designation lacks the specific LDC sub-type classification required by LDC § 25-2-3. The Site Data Table and application must explicitly identify the use as either 'Multifamily Residential', 'Condominium Residential', or 'Townhouse Residential'. Generic designations or variations of these terms (e.g., 'Multi-Family Residential', 'Residential', 'Apartments', 'Townhomes') are not acceptable. Clarify and update all documents to specify which of the three residential sub-types applies to this project.

Adjacent property uses are not labeled using LDC-defined use classifications. Site plan shows adjacent properties identified as 'Existing Apartment Building' and 'Clarion Ridge Condominiums' or by zoning designation only (SF-3, MF-3-CO). These must be relabeled with specific LDC use types: 'Multifamily Residential' for apartment complexes, 'Condominium Residential' for condominium projects, 'Single Family Residential' for single-family areas, and appropriate commercial/office/industrial classifications per LDC §§ 25-2-4 and 25-2-5 for other uses. Update site plan to replace zoning codes and descriptive project names with proper LDC use classifications for all adjacent properties.

Building elevation drawings are not included in the bound plan set. All height information is presented only in tabular form on Sheet 9; architectural elevation sheets showing building facades, dimensions, and measurement methodology are required.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the eight buildings on the site. Elevation drawings must be provided for all buildings and for all required sides of each building to verify height measurement, AAG calculation, and roof type-specific measurement methodology.

The site includes three distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex), but separate architectural elevation sheets are not provided for each type. Separate elevation sheets must be provided to document height, measurement methodology, and AAG calculation for each distinct building type.

The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values for each building, but does not explicitly show the AAG calculation formula (highest adjacent grade + lowest adjacent grade) ÷ 2, nor does it identify and label the highest and lowest grade points at each building perimeter. Elevation sheets must include the complete AAG calculation per LDC § 25-1-21(50).

The height measurement method cannot be verified from the site plan. No roof types (flat, pitched/hip, mansard, other) are designated on the site plan or in any drawings, and no measurement endpoints are specified. Elevation sheets must identify the roof type and show the applicable measurement point per LDC § 25-1-21(50): flat roof to top of coping; pitched/hip roof to average height of highest gable; mansard roof to deck line; other roof styles to highest point.

Compatibility height limit compliance cannot be verified. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061 (MF-2 zoning within 75 feet of SF-3 triggering property). The applicable limits are: 40 feet maximum within 50 feet of triggering property; 60 feet maximum between 50–75 feet. However, the site plan does not show distance zone boundaries, does not identify the adjacent SF-3 property line, and does not document building locations relative to the triggering property. Distance zone notation and cross-sectional documentation are required to verify compliance.
applicableAreas: all eight buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

comment: Compatibility distance zone boundaries are not shown on the site plan or elevation drawings. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061. Elevation drawings must show the 50-foot and 75-foot distance zone boundary lines from the SF-3 triggering property and dashed reference lines at the applicable maximum permitted heights (40 feet within the 50-foot zone; 60 feet in the 50–75-foot zone) to graphically demonstrate compliance.
applicableAreas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

comment: Cross-sectional elevation views are not provided. A cross-section is required showing the building profile relative to the SF-3 triggering property line, with distance zone boundaries (50-foot and 75-foot) clearly labeled, proposed building heights in each zone, and maximum allowed heights for each zone, all drawn to scale with dimensions labeled. This graphical representation is necessary to verify compliance with Article 10 compatibility height limits per LDC § 25-2-1061.
applicableAreas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

comment: Required zoning district setback lines (front, rear, interior side, street side) per LDC § 25-2-492 are not shown, labeled, or dimensioned on the site plan. While informal distance dimensions appear from property lines to buildings (19.3', 25', 21.3', 29.6', 46.9', 26.1', 25.8', 33.3'), these are not identified as setback requirement lines with corresponding code citations or identification of required distances. Setback lines must be clearly drawn and labeled with both the required distance and the applicable code section.
applicableAreas: site plan (Sheet 9) - all building setback lines

comment: Compatibility standards (Article 10) applicability cannot be definitively determined from submitted documents. Site is zoned MF-2 and is adjacent to an SF-3 parcel. New Article 10 (effective July 15, 2024) applies only to sites zoned MF-4 or less restrictive (MF-5, MF-6, commercial, industrial); MF-2 is more restrictive than MF-4 and therefore is not subject to new Article 10. Previous Subchapter F was completely repealed July 15, 2024. Since this plan was submitted May 20, 2025 (after framework change), applicability depends on whether regulatory transition provisions or alternative compatibility frameworks apply to MF-2 sites, which requires City staff clarification.

Transformer pad clearances cannot be verified. Four electrical transformer pads are proposed, but no clearance zones, dimension lines, or building construction type details are provided. Austin Energy Design Criteria 1.10.4 requires different clearances (5 ft for brick/masonry; 12 ft for non-masonry/mixed structures). Building construction types are not specified on the electrical plan, and no clearance radii or measurements are shown, preventing compliance verification.
applicableAreas: electrical transformer pads (Sheet 21) - 4 pads proposed at Bldgs 2, 4/5, 7/8

comment: Fire hydrant fence obstruction accounting cannot be verified. Wooden fence is shown on the Fire Protection Plan adjacent to the private fire hydrant, but fence height is not specified. Per Reviewer Convention, fencing 4 feet or greater in height must be accounted for in hydrant distance measurements. Without a specified height, it cannot be determined whether the fence constitutes an obstruction requiring measurement accommodation.
applicableAreas: wooden fence adjacent to fire hydrant near Bldg 7/8 (Sheet 10)

comment: Solid fence heights cannot be verified. Wooden privacy fences are shown along Northern, Eastern, and Southern property boundaries (designated H-6 in plan legend), but no fence heights are dimensioned or specified anywhere on the plan. LDC § 25-2-899(D) establishes 6-foot maximum height; § 25-2-899(E) permits 7 feet where grade change µ1 foot occurs. Without height dimensions, compliance with applicable maximum standards cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: wooden privacy fences at property lines (N, E, S boundaries) on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)

comment: Fence design details required by LDC § 25-2-899(I) are not shown on the Landscape Plan. Submittal date May 20, 2025 is after the July 31, 2023 effective date for design restrictions. The code prohibits: spiked pickets above the top horizontal backer rail; vertical pickets with 2-to-9-inch spacing above the top rail; razor wire; barbed wire (except airports); fences creating entrapment/impalement risk; and requires knuckle selvage for solid chain link. The plan must specify fence design and materials demonstrating compliance with these restrictions.
applicableAreas: wooden privacy fences at property lines (N, E, S boundaries) on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)

comment: Adjoining land uses not documented on all sides. South side shows 'Single Family' use without specific property identification. West side (Valley View Road street frontage) does not identify land uses across the street. East and north sides are labeled but incomplete documentation of all surrounding properties on all four sides.

Land uses for properties across adjacent streets and rights-of-way are not shown. Location map (Sheet 1) shows only street network. Site plan (Sheet 9) does not depict land uses across Valley View Road or other adjacent streets.

Adjacent property zoning district designations not shown on all sides. South side property is labeled with 'Use: Single Family' but no zoning designation is provided for this adjacent property. Zoning must be shown for all surrounding properties to verify compatibility requirements.

Adjacent zoning designations shown on site plan cannot be verified against current City GIS records. North property shown as 'MF-2-CO' but facts.md indicates adjacent SF-3 parcel (ID 0406100210). East side properties shown as 'MF-2-CO' with 'Claerain Ridge Condominiums' labeling. Zoning accuracy requires independent GIS confirmation.

Zoning designations not included on mylars. Sheet 2 (Plat) is the historical Mecey Subdivision recorded plat (1975) and does not include current zoning information. No current zoning notation is evident on the mylar/plat documents.

Existing building footprints on adjoining properties within 50 feet may not be completely shown. East side shows existing apartment buildings in dashed outline with annotations ('Existing 4-Story Brick Apt. Bldg.' height 45'-10"). North and south sides show no building footprints, but it is unclear whether buildings exist on these adjacent properties and are simply not depicted or whether no buildings exist. Documentation is incomplete or ambiguous.

Required note absent when no buildings exist on adjoining lots within 50 feet. North and south adjacent properties are shown without building footprints, but the site plan does not include the required notation: 'no buildings exist on adjoining lots within 50 feet.' If buildings exist on these properties, they must be depicted; if not, a required clarifying note must be added.

Dumpster or permanently placed refuse receptacle location not identified on site plan to verify 20-foot setback from properties zoned or used as SF-5 or more restrictive (LA, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5). Sheet 9 references trash collection requirements but does not depict the location of refuse receptacles on the site plan drawing. Compliance cannot be verified.

Residential parking (88 spaces: 10 surface + 78 garage) screening requirements cannot be fully verified. East adjacent property is zoned/used as Multi-Family (MF-2-CO residential). If this parking abuts the adjacent residential property, a wall, fence, or landscape screen at least 6 feet in height is required (LDC § 25-6-563(B)). Site plan shows wooden privacy fence on east side (H.6) but the HEIGHT of this fence is not specified on either the landscape plan or site plan. Compliance cannot be verified without fence height documentation.

Exterior lighting above the second floor is not verified to be absent where facing adjacent residential property. Sheet 9 notes state that 'All site lighting to be located on the building will be in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5 and will be reviewed during building plan review.' Individual luminaire locations and orientations above the second floor are not shown on the site plan. Compliance cannot be verified from submitted site plan; requires architectural/building elevation review.

Mechanical equipment noise level not demonstrated. No mechanical equipment schedule or noise specifications (dB(A)) at property lines adjacent to residential uses are provided on the site plan. Requirement applies to all sites with mechanical equipment adjacent to residential: noise may not exceed 70 dB(A) at the property line. Compliance cannot be verified without equipment schedule and noise ratings.

Open space area is labeled with total square footage (4,710 sf) but specific width, depth, and length dimensions are not provided. Only total area is dimensioned; individual linear dimensions must be shown for the open space boundaries.

The H.5 'Private Common Open Space' hatch pattern is defined in the Key Notes legend on Sheet 31 but is not applied to any area on the actual landscape plan drawing. The open space must be delineated with the appropriate hatch pattern or legend label to match the site plan delineation.

Square footage for common open space shown on plans is inconsistent. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 4,710 sf provided, but Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations) shows 5,855 sf provided. This 1,145 sf discrepancy must be resolved with consistent documentation across all plan sheets.

Open space percentages and delineation are inconsistent across plan sheets. Sheet 9 shows 4,710 sf (5.0% of site area); Sheet 35 shows 5,855 sf (6.2% of site area); Sheet 31 landscape plan does not delineate the open space at all despite being identified in the legend. All sheets must show consistent square footage and graphically represent the same open space area.

Type of open space is not identified on site plan. The area is labeled 'Common Open Space' but does not identify which of the 11 permitted types it represents: (1) natural and undeveloped, (2) landscaped area, (3) plaza or patio with outdoor seating, (4) play area, (5) educational/cultural/sensory feature, (6) swimming pool, (7) water quality/detention pond, (8) multi-use trail, (9) sports court, (10) transit plaza, or (11) combination. Explicit type designation is required.
applicableAreas: Common open space area on site plan

comment: Cannot verify whether open space meets Subchapter E minimum dimensional requirements (20 ft minimum width and depth, 650 SF minimum area) because the specific width and depth dimensions are not provided on the site plan. If the open space is claimed as a plaza or landscaped area type, these dimensions must be verified; currently only the total area (4,710 sf) is dimensioned.

Pedestrian amenities are not identified or shown within the open space areas. The site plan shows only tree symbols and hatching within the central open space courtyard, with no labeled seating, benches, tables, gathering areas, shade structures, or other pedestrian amenities. Required amenities must be identified and depicted on both site plan and landscape plan sheets.

Site area of 2.16 acres exceeds the 1-acre trigger for closed municipal solid waste landfill buffer compliance under LDC § 25-1-85. While topography, existing structures, and drainage patterns are generally shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) and ESCP (Sheet 5), the two perpetual easements (Greenbelt Access and City of Austin Drainage) that affect existing site conditions are not labeled or depicted on these sheets. These must be shown and labeled as existing recorded encumbrances affecting the permitted site boundary.

Above-grade features affecting drainage patterns (buildings, retaining walls, utility infrastructure) are depicted on ESCP and site plan sheets; however, the depiction of how the two perpetual easement areas (Greenbelt and Drainage) relate to drainage infrastructure and grading cannot be fully verified without these easement boundaries being shown. The relationship between proposed grading, drainage design, and the easement constraints must be clearly demonstrated.
